Chagrin Falls' Shade Tree Commission & Tree Permit

Chagrin Falls has an active Shade Tree Commission that reviews tree work involving the public right-of-way and historic-district properties, and a tree-protection ordinance that requires a permit for healthy-tree removal above a set DBH threshold. Roubic coordinates the village permit and commission review process in-house as part of the job — we know the village contacts, the application forms, and the review timelines.

Hazard trees (dead or dying) follow an expedited process with arborist documentation. Permit fees, when they apply, are billed at cost with no markup and disclosed upfront — no surprise charges.

Permit coordination included in every Chagrin Falls removal estimate at no separate fee

EAB Ash Stability Degradation

EAB has killed an estimated 90%+ of NE Ohio's ash. Standing dead ash in Chagrin Falls turns brittle within 18–24 months and fails violently in storms — the remaining dead trees are the fragile ones.

Wind-Load Failures

Chagrin Falls' mature ornamental canopy and ravine-edge trees take hard wind hits every spring. Leaning or dead-crown trees near structures become insurance-deductible events.

Right-of-Way & Ordinance Notices

Trees threatening the Chagrin Falls right-of-way or covered by the tree-protection ordinance can draw village notices if left unaddressed. The removal cost stays the same; the compliance delay does not.

Common Chagrin Falls Removal Questions

Chagrin Falls Tree Removal FAQ

Six things Chagrin Falls homeowners want to know before booking.

How much does tree removal cost in Chagrin Falls?
Tree removal in Chagrin Falls typically runs $400–$5,000+ depending on tree size, species, access, and any permit fees. Roubic's confirmed brackets: small tree under 30 ft $400–$800; medium 30–60 ft $650–$950; large 60–80 ft heritage oak $850–$2,000; very-large or crane-required 80+ ft $2,000–$5,000+. Emergency and after-hours work carries roughly a 30% premium. Every estimate is free and on-site.
Do I need a tree-removal permit in Chagrin Falls?
Chagrin Falls has a tree-protection ordinance requiring a permit for healthy-tree removal above a set DBH threshold, and an active Shade Tree Commission that reviews right-of-way and historic-district work. Roubic assesses DBH before quoting and coordinates the village permit and commission review on your behalf — hazard trees (dead or dying) follow an expedited process. There is no separate handling fee; only the village's actual permit cost passes through.
How quickly can Roubic remove a tree in Chagrin Falls?
Chagrin Falls is a Tier 1 Roubic service area. Standard removals are typically scheduled within 1–3 business days of estimate sign-off. Active emergencies (tree on structure, blocking a driveway, or a leaning hazard) get next-day or priority response from our Auburn Township yard, just 4 miles away. Call {{global.phone}} for emergency dispatch.
Will Roubic remove an EAB-killed ash tree in Chagrin Falls?
Yes. Emerald Ash Borer has killed an estimated 90%+ of ash trees in NE Ohio — including Chagrin Falls — since the 2008–2012 outbreak. EAB-killed ash become brittle within 18–24 months and fail violently in storms. We've removed hundreds of EAB-killed ash across the Chagrin Falls area; the wood enters our Auburn Township firewood yard for seasoning.
What if the tree I need removed is near a house, fence, or power line?
Tight-access removals in Chagrin Falls are routine for our crews. We use sectional dismantling with rigging when bucket-truck access is limited, crane support for heritage trees near structures, and direct coordination with FirstEnergy / The Illuminating Company when work intersects power lines. Insurance documentation is built into every job involving property-protection scenarios.
Can Roubic remove a ravine-edge tree with no driveway or bucket-truck access?
Yes — ravine-edge and no-access removals along the Chagrin River are common here. We use climbing-based sectional removal with rigging where bucket trucks can't reach, mat protection on soft or sloped approaches, and crane support when a tree sits near a structure. Aaron confirms the exact approach during the free on-site estimate walk.
